facts.statement: Punatitan is a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation in La Rioja, Argentina.
facts.quote: Punatitan (meaning "puna giant") is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation of La Rioja, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Punatitan contains only one known species, Punatitan coughlini.
facts.quote: It contains one species, Punatitan coughlini.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including cervical and dorsal vertebrae, a partial sacrum, 13 articulated tail vertebrae, and pelvic and rib fragments.
facts.quote: a partial skeleton composed of the anterior portion of posterior cervical vertebra (likely C12), two middle dorsal vertebrae (likely D6–D7), a partial sacrum, 13 articulated caudal vertebrae (some with articulated haemal arches), the right pubis, the left ischium, and several dorsal ribs

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Punatitan as a derived member of the Lithostrotia within the clade Aeolosaurini, a subclade of Rinconsauria.
facts.quote: The describers' phylogenetic analysis places Punatitan as a derived member of the Lithostrotia, in the clade Aeolosaurini, which they recover as a subclade of Rinconsauria

facts.statement: Although Punatitan was recovered within a clade containing two Aeolosaurus species, researchers did not assign it to that genus due to doubts regarding the placement of Aeolosaurus maximus.
facts.quote: Notably, Punatitan was recovered within a clade consisting of two species of the genus Aeolosaurus, but the describers refrained from assigning it to said genus, instead regarding the more basal species' ("A." maximus) placement in Aeolosaurus dubious.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest a possible connection between Punatitan and the contemporary Bravasaurus regarding the titanosaur egg concentration found at the site.
facts.quote: The describing authors suggest some connection with either Punatitan or its contemporary Bravasaurus, which was described in the same paper.

facts.statement: Punatitan lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
